findings.fix: Add an explicit conclusion-signalling phrase at the point the artifact states its central claim, for example "therefore" or "we recommend".
findings.location: the whole document, under its "Ending Overdue Fines Systemwide: A Recommendation" heading
findings.violation: No phrase from the conclusion-marker lexicon (therefore, thus, hence, it follows that, we recommend, this paper argues, I argue that, the conclusion is, in conclusion, we should, the case for) appears anywhere in the artifact, so a reader scanning rather than reading straight through has no signpost to where the conclusion is asserted.

findings.evidence: The Recommendation section reads "Given the return-rate and avoidance-survey results above" and the prior section reads "the pilot's return-rate and avoidance-survey results, taken together, support ending fines," but "## What the Pilot Showed" (the section that would carry the pilot results) presents only the avoidance-survey figures (20 percent to 3 percent); no return-rate figure, percentage, or description appears anywhere in the artifact.
findings.fix: Either add the pilot's actual return-rate figures (before/after on-time return percentages at the pilot branches) to "## What the Pilot Showed," or stop citing "return-rate results" as part of the grounds everywhere it is invoked.
findings.location: "## What the Pilot Showed" and "## Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide" sections
findings.violation: The central claim's stated evidentiary basis names two results, return-rate and avoidance-survey, and treats both as already shown ("above"), but only the avoidance-survey result is actually present in the document; a reader checking the "return-rate" plank finds nothing to examine.

findings.evidence: 10 of 14 sentences (0.71) carry at least one hedging term.
findings.fix: Remove the hedge from sentences whose claim the evidence actually supports, reserving qualification for the claims that genuinely need it.
findings.location: the whole document, under its "Ending Overdue Fines Systemwide: A Recommendation" heading
findings.violation: More than 0.35 of the artifact's sentences carry a term from the hedging lexicon (may, might, could, possibly, perhaps, arguably, somewhat, relatively, it seems, appears to, tends to, to a degree), spread across the whole document rather than concentrated where the evidence actually underdetermines the claim.

findings.evidence: "Ending overdue fines is plainly the better path for the consortium, and delaying the change would only cost every branch more." and "This recommendation removes every overdue-related charge permanently, for every item the consortium owns, without qualification."
findings.fix: Replace the absolute language with wording scaled to a single-pilot, partial-evidence result (e.g., "the pilot results suggest" rather than "plainly"; drop "permanently" and "without qualification" or state the conditions under which the policy would be revisited).
findings.location: "## What the Pilot Showed" opening sentence and "## Recommendation" closing sentence
findings.violation: The claim is asserted at maximum strength ("plainly," "only cost... more," "permanently," "without qualification") while the grounds behind it are a single avoidance-survey at four of ten branches over twelve months, with the companion return-rate evidence absent from the document entirely (see TOULMIN-GROUNDS); a reader acting on the stated certainty has no signal that the result might not generalize or that a downside case was never tested.

findings.evidence: "removing the financial penalty for late returns predictably increases both on-time return rates and overall program participation" is backed by "the Tri-County Library Data Cooperative's 2023 fines-elimination research brief, which reviewed return-rate data from fourteen library systems that eliminated fines between 2017 and 2022."
findings.fix: Either name a source for the participation effect (a study, internal data, or precedent showing program participation rose) or drop "overall program participation" from the stated principle so the warrant claims only what its backing supports.
findings.location: "## Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide" section, second paragraph
findings.violation: The warrant asserts two effects, increased return rates and increased "overall program participation," but the named backing is described only as reviewing "return-rate data"; the participation half of the principle is never attached to any study, standard, or body of practice, so a target reader has nothing to test that half of the claim against while the return-rate half stays checkable.

findings.evidence: "the stronger choice is a systemwide end to overdue fines across all ten consortium branches, effective at the start of the next fiscal year." is immediately followed by "Specifically, the recommended change is about making things better for patrons going forward, in whatever way the consortium finds workable."
findings.fix: Delete the "Specifically..." sentence, or replace it with language that narrows the first sentence's claim rather than widening it into an open-ended aspiration.
findings.violation: A crisp, specific conclusion is stated and then immediately dissolved into a vacuous restatement introduced as its specification ("Specifically..."); a reader cannot tell whether the ask is the dated, ten-branch fine elimination or the open-ended "whatever way the consortium finds workable," which only reduces to the first if the reader discards the sentence that claims to specify it.

findings.evidence: The artifact raises and answers the revenue objection ("a skeptic on the board points to overdue fines as a source of materials-replacement funding" -> answered with finance-record figures), but nowhere raises or answers the objection that the recommendation's scope ("every overdue-related charge permanently, for every item the consortium owns, without qualification") exceeds what the pilot tested (fines specifically, at four of ten branches).
findings.fix: Add a section or paragraph addressing why the pilot's fines-specific result justifies eliminating every overdue-related charge rather than fines alone, or narrow the recommendation's scope to match what was piloted.
findings.location: "## Addressing the Revenue Concern" versus "## Recommendation"
findings.violation: The artifact anticipates and answers one foreseeable challenge (revenue) but leaves a second one its own grounds expose, the scope gap between a fines-only pilot and a permanent, unqualified, all-charges systemwide policy, unraised and unanswered.

findings.evidence: The stated principle is "removing the financial penalty for late returns predictably increases both on-time return rates and overall program participation"; the recommendation it is offered to license is "removes every overdue-related charge permanently, for every item the consortium owns, without qualification."
findings.fix: Either narrow the Recommendation section's language to match the warrant's actual scope (ending overdue fines) or state a principle broad enough to cover every overdue-related charge, permanently and without qualification.
findings.location: "## Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide" versus "## Recommendation"
findings.violation: The warrant licenses ending the late-return financial penalty, i.e., fines; it does not by its own wording license eliminating every overdue-related charge (which can reasonably include charges other than late-return fines, such as replacement costs) on a permanent, unqualified basis, so the conclusion actually drawn is broader than the stated principle supports.
